title: Reverse Exchange Coordination
name: Reverse Exchange Coordination
metaTitle: Reverse Exchange Coordination in Oklahoma City, OK
metaDescription: We coordinate the exchange accommodation titleholder structure for reverse 1031 exchanges in Oklahoma City when replacement property comes up first.

sections.html: Sometimes the right replacement property in Oklahoma City shows up before your relinquished property is even under contract, and that's when a reverse exchange structure matters instead of a standard forward one. We coordinate the exchange accommodation titleholder arrangement, the parking of title, and the eventual sale of your relinquished property so the sequence holds up if it's ever examined. It's a heavier lift than a forward exchange, and we treat it that way from the first phone call.

sections.heading: Why the Title Has to Park Somewhere Else First
sections.html:
You can't hold title to both the relinquished and replacement property at the same time and still complete a valid exchange, so an exchange accommodation titleholder, or EAT, takes and holds title to one of the two properties temporarily. That arrangement is set up through a qualified exchange accommodation agreement before any property changes hands, and getting the sequence right at the start is what keeps the structure standing up later if it's ever reviewed.

We work with your qualified intermediary to select an EAT structure that fits the specific property and financing situation, rather than defaulting to whatever the last transaction used.

sections.heading: What We Coordinate While Title Sits With the EAT
sections.html:
While the EAT holds title, several practical pieces have to keep moving on schedule, and we track each one:

  • Financing arrangements for the parked property, since most lenders won't lend directly to the EAT
  • Property management and maintenance responsibility while title sits outside your name
  • Insurance coverage naming the correct party during the parking period
  • Tax and expense pass-through arrangements between you and the EAT
  • Identification of which property will ultimately be treated as relinquished, inside the 45-day window
  • The 180-day deadline for completing the exchange from the parking date

We check in on each of these on a set schedule rather than waiting for a problem to surface.

sections.heading: Running the Building Like You Own It, Even When You Don't Yet
sections.html: Tenant communication, vendor invoices, and service contracts don't pause just because title is technically parked with an accommodation titleholder. We coordinate those practical operations the same way you'd manage them if the deed already had your name on it, since the building still needs to run day to day while the paperwork catches up behind the scenes.

sections.heading: Where Reverse Exchanges Get More Expensive Than Forward Ones
sections.html:
EAT fees, financing complexity, and insurance structuring all add cost compared to a standard forward exchange, so we help you weigh whether the timing benefit of locking in a strong Oklahoma City property is worth the added coordination expense. For some deals, particularly thinner-margin ones, a forward exchange with a tighter sourcing timeline may make more sense than parking title at all.

We lay out the added cost items early, before you commit to the structure, so the decision is made with real numbers instead of after the EAT arrangement is already in motion.

sections.heading: Coordinating the Eventual Sale of Your Relinquished Property
sections.html: Once the replacement property's title is parked, you still have to complete the sale of your relinquished property inside the reverse exchange structure's window. We track that sale process alongside the parking arrangement so the entire sequence closes cleanly, rather than treating the two sides of the transaction as separate projects running on their own timelines.

faqs.q: What is an exchange accommodation titleholder and why is it needed?
faqs.a: An exchange accommodation titleholder is a party that temporarily holds title to either your replacement or relinquished property because you can't hold both simultaneously and still complete a valid reverse exchange. The arrangement is set up through a formal agreement before any property changes hands, and we help select the structure that fits your specific deal and financing situation.

faqs.q: Can I get a conventional loan on a property while title sits with the EAT?
faqs.a: Most conventional lenders won't lend directly to an EAT, so reverse exchange financing typically requires either a lender familiar with the structure or a different financing approach entirely. We coordinate this early since it affects the whole timeline and can change which properties are realistic candidates for a reverse structure in the first place.

faqs.q: Does the 180-day deadline work differently in a reverse exchange?
faqs.a: The 180-day period still applies, but it runs from the date title is parked with the EAT rather than from a relinquished property closing, which is the reverse of how a forward exchange calculates the deadline. Confirm the exact dates with your qualified intermediary before you rely on any timeline assumption, since a miscalculated start date can quietly shrink the amount of time you thought you had to work with.

faqs.q: Who manages the property while title is parked with the EAT?
faqs.a: Practical property management, including tenant communication and vendor contracts, is typically coordinated by you or your management team even while the EAT holds legal title. We help structure that so day-to-day operations don't stall during the parking period while the paperwork is being finalized, and we confirm insurance and liability coverage names the right party throughout.

faqs.q: Why do reverse exchanges cost more than a standard forward exchange?
faqs.a: Additional legal structuring, EAT fees, and financing complexity all add cost that a standard forward exchange doesn't carry. We walk through those added costs against the benefit of locking in a property before your relinquished asset sells, so you can decide if the tradeoff makes sense given your specific timeline, budget, and overall financing situation before you commit to the structure.
